transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… well, because people keep telling me I’m making something out of nothing, but I’m not. I know what I’m seeing. The hospital people, and some people from the agency I work with, they’ve been watching our house and even the routes I take when I’m cleaning. It’s like they’re checking up on me, making sure I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I know how that sounds when I say it out loud, but it’s been going on enough that I can’t just ignore it. People act like I’m imagining it or being dramatic, but there are little things—where they show up, how they look at me, how things seem to line up. I just need someone to take me seriously, because it feels like everybody is watching and judging what I’m doing.
Do you think these people are watching you for a specific reason?

Yes. I think they’re watching because they want to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. That’s what it feels like. Like the hospital people, and some of the people from the agency I work with, they’re not just randomly around—they’re checking up on me.

It’s not just at the house, either. It’s along the routes I take when I’m cleaning, like they know where I’m supposed to be. And then people act like I’m imagining it, like I’m making it bigger than it is, but I know what I’m seeing. It’s the looks, the timing, how they show up in certain places. It’s like they’re judging whether I’m doing things right for him.
Do you think these people are actually working together to watch you?

I mean… yes, I do think there’s some kind of working together, or at least they’re all aware of it. I don’t know if they sit in a room and plan it out, you know, but it doesn’t feel separate to me. The hospital people and some of the agency people, they show up in ways that are too convenient, too lined up with where I am and what I’m doing.

Like, it’s not just someone passing by one time. It’s the house, and then it’s the places I go on my cleaning routes, and the way they look at me like they already know something. And people keep saying I’m imagining it, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It feels like they’re watching to make sure I’m taking care of my husband the right way, like they’re checking up on me together and judging everything.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't believe people were watching you?

I mean… before all this, I didn’t think about people watching me like this all the time. I was just going to work, cleaning houses, taking care of things at home, taking care of my husband. But lately it’s hard to believe it’s not happening, because it’s not just a feeling out of nowhere.

People keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people, and some of the people from the agency, they’ve been around the house and even along my cleaning routes. It feels like they’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. So maybe there were times before when I didn’t believe it, but now… no, now I can’t just ignore it. It lines up too much.
Do you ever have days where you don't think people are watching you?

Not really… I mean, maybe there are moments when I’m busy enough that I’m not thinking about it every second, like if I’m scrubbing something or trying to get through a job, but then something happens and it comes right back. Somebody’s there near the house, or I notice someone along one of my cleaning routes, and it’s the way they look at me, like they already know what they’re checking for.

That’s why I’m here, because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m making it up or seeing things wrong, but I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people and some of the folks from the agency, they’ve been watching our house and where I go for work. It feels like they’re trying to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband, like I’m being judged. So no, I don’t really have a whole day where I think, “Oh, nobody’s watching.” It’s hard to let that go when it keeps lining up that way.
Do you ever think that maybe you're misinterpreting these signs and that people are not actually watching you?

I’ve tried to think that, because everybody keeps saying that’s what it is, that I’m reading into things or I’m imagining it. I do hear that. But then I go back to what I’ve actually seen, and it doesn’t feel like just a mistake.

I mean, the hospital people and some of the agency people, they’ve been around our house, and then I’ll see people connected to it along my cleaning routes too. It’s not like one odd look from one stranger. It’s the same kind of watching, the same feeling that they already know about me and my husband, like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of him. And that’s why I’m here, because people keep acting like I’m making it up, but I know what I’ve been seeing.

So… could someone say I’m misinterpreting it? Yes, they could say that. But I don’t really believe that’s what’s happening. It lines up too much for me to just brush it off.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be wrong about people watching you?

I mean… I guess if you’re asking me to say is there any tiny possibility, I can say maybe, because I know people keep telling me that. I’m not trying to be difficult. I understand what you’re asking. But in my mind, it doesn’t feel like I’m wrong.

That’s part of why I’m here, because everyone keeps acting like I’m imagining it or making connections that aren’t there. But I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people and some of the people from the agency have been around our house, and then I see them—or people connected with them—around my cleaning routes too. And it feels very clear to me that they’re watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So… could I be wrong in the way other people keep saying? I don’t really believe that. It’s happened too many times, in too many places, for me to just say, “Oh, that’s nothing.”
Do you think you will ever stop believing that people are watching you?

I don’t know… I mean, I’d like to stop feeling like this, because it’s exhausting, honestly. I don’t want to be going around thinking about who’s outside the house or who I might see when I’m out cleaning. I don’t enjoy it. It makes everything harder.

But if you’re asking whether I think I’ll just stop believing it, like wake up one day and say, “Oh, none of that was real,” I don’t really see how I could do that when I know what I’ve seen. That’s the part people don’t seem to understand. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’ve made the whole thing up in my head, but the hospital people and some of those folks from the agency have been watching our house, and I’ve seen signs of it on my cleaning routes too. It feels like they’re checking up on me, watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So… I don’t know if I’ll ever stop believing it unless they stop, or unless someone can really explain why all these things keep happening in a way that makes sense. I’m not trying to hold onto it. I just can’t pretend I don’t know what’s going on.
Do you think you will ever be able to completely stop thinking that people are watching you?

Completely stop? I don’t know. I mean, I wish I could, because it wears me down, thinking about it all the time, wondering who’s there and what they’re looking for. But it’s hard to just stop thinking something when it keeps feeling like it’s right in front of you.

I know people keep acting like I’m imagining it, and that’s partly why I’m here, because everybody wants me to question it or say maybe I’m wrong. But I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people, and some of those folks from the agency, they’ve been watching around our house, and I’ve noticed the same kind of thing on my cleaning routes too. It feels like they’re checking on whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So if you mean could I completely stop thinking it on my own… I don’t see how, not while it keeps happening. Maybe if they stopped coming around, or if there was some explanation that actually made sense, maybe then I could let it go. But right now, no, I can’t just shut it off and pretend I don’t know what I know.
Do you think your belief that people are watching you could ever change?

Could it change… I mean, I suppose anything could change if something actually changed, you know? I’m not saying I want to feel watched forever. I don’t. It’s tiring, and it makes me feel like I’m always having to explain myself.

But right now, I don’t see how the belief would just change when I’m here because people keep telling me I’m imagining it, and that doesn’t match what I’ve seen. The hospital people and some of those people from the agency have been around our house, and I’ve seen things on my cleaning routes too, like they’re connected to it, like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So if you mean could I be convinced someday, I don’t know. Maybe if there was a real explanation that made sense, or if they stopped showing up, maybe I could think about it differently. But right now it doesn’t feel like just a belief to me. It feels like something that’s happening.
Do you think there's anything that could happen that would make you completely change your mind about people watching you?

I mean… completely change my mind? That’s hard for me to answer, because it’s not like I just decided one day to think this. I know people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m making connections where there aren’t any, but I’ve seen enough that it doesn’t feel like something I can just set down because someone tells me to.

Maybe if someone could really show me, not just say it, but show me in a way that made sense why the hospital people were around, and why those agency folks seemed to be watching the house, and why I keep noticing the same kind of thing when I’m out on my cleaning routes… maybe then I could start to think differently. But it would have to explain all of it, not just one little piece.

Because from where I’m standing, it looks like they’re checking up on me, watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. And that hurts, too, because I do take care of him. So for me to completely change my mind, I’d need something pretty clear, something that actually accounts for what I’ve seen. Otherwise I don’t know how I’m supposed to just say, “Oh, I was wrong,” when it still feels like it’s happening.
Do you think there's anything that could make you doubt your belief that people are watching you?

Doubt it… I mean, I guess maybe, if someone could really explain it in a way that fit everything I’ve noticed. Not just tell me, “Oh, you’re imagining things,” because that’s what people keep doing, and that doesn’t help me doubt it. It actually makes me feel more like they’re trying to brush it off.

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m making it up or seeing something that isn’t there, but I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people have been around, and some of those agency folks too, around our house, and then I notice things on my cleaning routes, like it follows into my work somehow. It’s not just one strange thing one time. It’s the way it keeps happening, the way it feels connected, like they’re watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So could something make me doubt it? Maybe if there was a clear reason for all of it, something that made sense and didn’t ignore the parts I’ve already seen. But just somebody saying, “No, that’s not happening,” no. That doesn’t make me doubt it. Not when it still feels like they’re watching.
Do you think your beliefs about being watched could be part of a larger idea or story that explains everything that's happening to you?

Yes… I mean, that’s sort of how it feels to me, I guess. Not like a “story” I made up, though. I don’t like saying it that way, because it makes it sound like I’m sitting around inventing things. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but to me the pieces line up.

The hospital people, and then some of those folks from the agency being around our house, and then things I notice when I’m out on my cleaning routes… it doesn’t feel separate. It feels connected, like there’s this bigger reason behind it, like they’re watching to see whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. And I know people say, “Well, maybe that’s just coincidence,” but when it keeps happening in different places, it doesn’t feel like coincidence to me.

So yes, I suppose it does explain what’s been happening. It explains why I feel checked on, why certain people are around, why I keep noticing them. I’m not trying to make trouble. I just feel like everyone wants me to ignore what’s right in front of me.
Do you think there's anything that could change your mind about the people watching you, or is that something you feel is absolutely true?

I wouldn’t say there’s nothing that could ever change my mind, because I’m trying to be fair, you know? I know you’re asking if I think it’s absolutely true, and… from where I’m sitting, it feels true. It doesn’t feel like just a thought I had and then decided to keep. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m taking ordinary things and making them into something else, but I know what I’ve seen.

The hospital people have been around, and some of those agency folks too, and it hasn’t just been at the house. I’ve noticed things when I’m out doing my cleaning routes too, like it follows into different parts of my day. That’s what makes it hard for me to just say, “Maybe it’s nothing.” If it were one time, maybe I could brush it off, but when it keeps showing up around the house and around my work, it feels like they’re watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

So… could something change my mind? Maybe if someone could explain all of that in a way that actually made sense and didn’t just dismiss me. But right now, no, I don’t feel like I’m wrong about it. I feel like people are watching, and I feel like everyone wants me to act like I don’t notice.
Do you think there is anything that could ever make you completely stop believing that people are watching you?

Completely stop believing it? I don’t know… that’s hard for me to say, because if I say “yes,” it sounds like I’m admitting it’s all in my head, and that’s not what I mean. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m making something out of nothing, but I know what I’ve seen.

It’s not just one person walking by or one car parked somewhere. It’s the hospital people, and some of those agency folks, around our house, and then I notice things on my cleaning routes too. That’s the part people don’t seem to understand. It’s like it follows from home into work, and it feels like they’re watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. So for me to completely stop believing it, someone would have to explain all of that in a way that actually fits, not just say, “You’re imagining it.”

I guess if there was real proof, or if someone could sit down and show me why those people were there, why it keeps happening around the house and when I’m out cleaning, maybe… maybe I could start to let go of it. But right now, no, I can’t just completely stop believing it. It feels too real.
Do you think the people watching you are part of a bigger plan or scheme?

Yes… I think so. I don’t know if I’d call it a “scheme” exactly, because that sounds like I’m saying I know every person involved or I have some whole map of it, and I don’t. But it feels bigger than just one person being nosy.

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people, and some of those agency folks, they’ve been around our house, and then I notice things when I’m out on my cleaning routes too. It’s not just at home, and that’s what makes it feel organized to me. Like they’re watching in different places to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I know how that sounds when I say it out loud. People look at me like I’m making connections that aren’t there. But when it keeps happening around the house and then follows into my workday, it’s hard not to think there’s a bigger plan behind it. Not like some movie or anything. More like… people checking up on me, maybe reporting back, trying to catch me doing something wrong. That’s what it feels like.
Do you think you will ever be able to forget about the people watching you or will it always be on your mind?

I don’t think I can just forget about it, no. I wish I could say I could put it out of my mind, because honestly it’s tiring to keep noticing things and wondering what they mean. But when it’s about my house and my husband, it’s not something I can just shrug off.

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, like I’m taking it too seriously, but I know what I’ve seen. It’s not just one little thing. It’s the hospital people, and some of those agency folks, being around our house, and then I notice things when I’m out doing my cleaning routes too. So it’s not like I can leave the house and it goes away. It follows me in my mind because it feels like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

Maybe if it stopped completely, or if someone gave me a real explanation that made sense, then maybe it wouldn’t be on my mind so much. But right now, I can’t forget about it. It’s there in the background even when I’m trying to do regular things, because I feel like I have to pay attention.
Do you think the people watching you are connected to any other events or situations in your life?

Yes, I do think it’s connected. I don’t think it’s just random people watching me for no reason. It feels connected to my husband, and whether people think I’m taking proper care of him.

That’s what I keep trying to explain. I’m here because people keep saying I’m imagining it, or that I’m reading too much into things, but I know what I’ve seen. It’s not just around the house, either. I’ve seen hospital people and some of the agency folks around our house, and then when I’m out doing my cleaning routes, I notice things there too. So it feels like it ties into both parts of my life — home and work.

At home, it’s like they’re checking up on me because of my husband. And then when I’m cleaning, I’ll notice certain people or situations and it feels like it follows me there too, like they’re still keeping an eye on me, maybe seeing if I’m responsible, if I’m doing things right. I know other people don’t see it the way I do, but to me it fits together. It’s connected to that whole situation of people judging whether I’m caring for him properly.
Do you think the people watching you fit into a larger story or explanation that makes sense of everything happening in your life?

Yes… that’s kind of how it feels to me. Like if I try to explain just one little thing, people say, “Well, maybe that was nothing,” or “Maybe you misunderstood.” But when I put it all together, it makes sense in a way that I can’t just ignore.

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know what I’ve seen. The hospital people, and some of those folks from the agency, they’ve been watching around our house. And it’s not just the house, either — I’ve noticed things when I’m out on my cleaning routes too. That’s what makes it feel like it’s part of a bigger explanation, not just random people looking at me.

To me, it all comes back to my husband. Like they’re trying to see whether I’m taking proper care of him, whether I’m doing something wrong, whether I’m responsible enough. I don’t have every detail, and I’m not saying I know exactly who told who to do what, but it fits together in my mind. The house, the agency people, the hospital people, even things I notice while I’m working — it all feels connected to them checking up on me.
Do you think your beliefs about being watched are unshakeable and cannot be changed by any argument or evidence?

I don’t know if I’d say “unshakeable” like I’m trying to be stubborn, because that makes it sound like I just decided this and won’t listen to anybody. I do listen. I hear what people say. People keep telling me I’m imagining it, or that I’m reading too much into things, or that maybe the people I saw were just there for some ordinary reason. I understand that’s what they think.

But from where I’m standing, I know what I’ve seen. It isn’t just one person one time. It’s the hospital people, and some of those agency folks, around our house, and then I notice things on my cleaning routes too. That’s why it’s hard for me to just accept someone saying, “No, that’s nothing.” Because it doesn’t feel like nothing when it keeps happening in different places.

If somebody had an explanation that actually fit everything, I’d try to hear it. I’m not saying I wouldn’t listen at all. But just arguing with me or telling me I’m imagining it doesn’t change it, because it feels too connected to my husband and whether they think I’m taking proper care of him. That’s the part people don’t seem to understand. To me, it makes sense that they’re checking on me. So no, it’s not easy to change my mind about it.
